segments.text: Okay so today we're going to take a look at how the internet is affecting cultures around the world.
Is it changing them in any way and if that's a good thing or not?
In particular I want you to come back to that question about westernisation.
Is the internet a one-way medium for westernisation?
Maybe Lucy would you like to start us off?
Okay, well, I don't think the internet is a force for good, really. I'd say it's certainly
having an impact, and that impact is the domination of other cultures by the West. Most of the
information on the net is English, and a lot of it is pop culture stuff, so it's too overwhelming.
It makes the young people who use the net in other countries forget about their own
cultures and try to imitate the West.
Well, I think it's true that it exposes people around the world to a lot of Western pop culture.
That's inevitable when so much of it is in the English language.
I suppose it's not just pop culture either.
I mean, most scientific information on the net is written in English too.
But I disagree with you Lucy that it's a bad thing.
There are obvious benefits from having this greater worldwide sense of sharing in a common
global culture. You know, more people agree about the important things like human rights and so on.
But that's a different thing, Simon. I agree that common values are a good thing,
but they don't have to be spread exclusively by the internet.
The internet is basically a pop culture thing, and for any good that it offers,
There are many other bad things. It helps to promote Western culture at the expense of
other cultures, which is unfair. It makes Western businesses stronger at the expense
of local businesses. And anyway, good values, like respect for the law or human rights or
things like that, they're not exclusively Western values. It's arrogant to think that
all that's good in the world comes from the west and other cultures need to learn it from
us somehow.
